claims.statement: A two-pass BODHI prompt raises the HealthBench Hard overall score of GPT-4.1-mini from 2.5% to 19.1% (+16.6 pp, 95% CI 15.5-17.7) and of GPT-4o-mini from 0.0% to 2.2% (+2.2 pp) on 200 vignettes x 5 seeds, at the cost of communication quality (-12.5 and -11.3 pp).
claims.scope: Two small OpenAI models, temperature 0.7, HealthBench Hard (200 cases), rubric-graded. No non-BODHI 'think first' two-pass control, so the gain is BODHI-vs-single-pass, not BODHI-vs-any-scaffold.

our_assessment.why: The risk differences are the informative numbers and they are reported. Missing: a matched two-pass control without the virtue content, which is what separates 'BODHI' from 'any chain-of-thought scaffold'.

claims.statement: BODHI achieves very large effect sizes on curiosity and humility: context-seeking Cohen's d = 16.38 (GPT-4.1-mini) and 19.54 (GPT-4o-mini), hedging d = 5.80, computed 'with Hedges' g correction'.
claims.scope: Table 1. Values shown as mean +- SD across five seeds.

our_assessment.why: All eight printed d values in Table 1 reproduce to within rounding as (difference of seed means) / (pooled SD of the five seed means), e.g. context-seeking 89.5 / sqrt((6.8^2+3.7^2)/2) = 16.35 vs 16.38 printed. So the standardiser is the seed-to-seed spread of a 200-case AVERAGE, which measures how reproducible the mean is, not how large the behavioural change is; d computed this way grows with cases per seed without the effect changing. Standardised per response, the same rates give 4.04 (context-seeking) and 0.66 (hedging, 'humility'), and 0.29 for GPT-4o-mini hedging. The Hedges' correction said to be applied is not visible either: with n = 5 per arm it would shrink 16.35 to 14.77. Separately, context-seeking is defined as 'at least one clarifying question' and the BODHI prompt instructs the model to produce '1-2 specific clarifying questions', so the curiosity metric is largely a manipulation check (did it follow the instruction), not an outcome. The +89.6 pp risk difference is real; the adjective 'very large effect on curiosity' is not supported by these numbers.

claims.statement: Seed-level SDs in Table 1 are larger than the binomial ceiling for 200 responses on fixed cases: 6.8 pp printed for the GPT-4.1-mini baseline context-seeking rate (mean 7.8%) against at most 1.9 pp if each seed re-samples responses on the same 200 vignettes.
claims.scope: Our derivation from Table 1; the supplement defining the seed procedure was not read.

our_assessment.why: Either seeds change which cases are drawn, or per-seed n is not 200, or 'SD' is something other than between-seed SD. Each has a different consequence for the CIs. The implied per-seed n differs across rows (about 16 for one, about 80 for another), so no single reading fits. Needs the supplement S3.
